prompt: explain what happens when a user enters a URL and a web page loads

keyLinks.effect: The browser looks up the server's IP address (DNS)
keyLinks.mechanism: Networks deliver data to numeric IP addresses, not to names, so the name must be translated first

keyLinks.effect: The browser opens a connection to that server (TCP, plus a TLS handshake for HTTPS)
keyLinks.mechanism: A request can only be sent over an established connection

keyLinks.effect: The browser sends an HTTP request for the page
keyLinks.mechanism: The request says which page is wanted

keyLinks.effect: The server sends back a response containing the HTML
keyLinks.mechanism: The server finds or builds the page and replies with a status and body

keyLinks.effect: The browser requests further resources (CSS, JavaScript, images)
keyLinks.mechanism: The HTML references other files that are fetched separately

keyLinks.cause: The browser has the HTML (and CSS)
keyLinks.effect: The browser builds and paints the page on screen
keyLinks.mechanism: It parses the markup, works out layout and styles, then draws pixels

knownErrors.claim: The name/URL goes straight to the server with no address lookup
knownErrors.why: Without resolving the name to an IP address the browser cannot reach the server

knownErrors.claim: "Page not found" (404) happens because the server did not respond
knownErrors.why: A 404 is itself a response from a reachable server; no response gives a timeout or "can't be reached"

knownErrors.claim: The server sends a finished picture/screenshot of the page
knownErrors.why: The server sends HTML and other files; the browser builds and draws the page itself

knownErrors.claim: "Site can't be reached" is caused by a wrong page path
knownErrors.why: That error comes from failing to resolve or connect; a wrong path on a reachable server gives a 404

acceptableSimplifications: Calling DNS a phone book or address book
Omitting caching, CDNs, redirects and TCP/TLS details
Merging parsing, layout and painting into one step
